context: A uni student interviews a doctor about clinical research
purpose: Teach: 矯正/救急/注射/生理/医薬品/探る/本能/許容

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生、本日はお忙しい中ありがとうございます。臨床研究について、医学生として伺いたいことがいくつかあります。
lines.en: Doctor, thank you for your time today. As a medical student, I have several questions about clinical research.
lines.style: Polite formal opening from earnest university student conducting interview.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: どうぞ、遠慮なく。新しい医薬品の開発には、若い世代の関心が欠かせませんからね。
lines.en: Please, don't hold back. The development of new pharmaceuticals requires the interest of younger generations.
lines.style: Warm encouraging tone from experienced doctor welcoming inquiry.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。例えば注射薬の治験では、被験者の生理的な反応をどのように観察されているのですか？
lines.en: Thank you. For example, in injection drug trials, how do you observe the physiological reactions of subjects?
lines.style: Curious academic question with specific clinical terminology used naturally.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 心拍や血圧を細かく記録して、許容範囲を超える変化があればすぐに中止します。安全が最優先ですよ。
lines.en: We record heart rate and blood pressure carefully, and stop immediately if changes exceed the permissible range. Safety comes first.
lines.style: Measured professional explanation emphasizing patient safety priorities.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。万が一の場合、救急対応の体制も整っているんですね。
lines.en: I see. So in case of emergencies, you also have emergency response systems in place.
lines.style: Understanding follow-up that builds on the doctor's previous explanation.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: もちろんです。それと、被験者の本能的な不安にも配慮しています。データだけでなく心も大切ですから。
lines.en: Of course. And we also consider the instinctive anxieties of subjects. It's not just data — the heart matters too.
lines.style: Compassionate explanation revealing humanistic side of medical research.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 心理面まで…。被験者の本音を探るのも、研究の一部なのでしょうか？
lines.en: Even the psychological aspect... Is exploring the true feelings of subjects also part of the research?
lines.style: Thoughtful probing question showing deeper engagement with the topic.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: そうですね。データの偏りを矯正するためにも、率直な声を聞くことは欠かせません。
lines.en: Yes, indeed. To correct biases in the data, listening to honest voices is indispensable.
lines.style: Reflective answer connecting interview methodology to research integrity.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今日は本当に勉強になりました。将来、私もそんな誠実な医師になりたいです。
lines.en: I really learned a lot today. In the future, I want to become such a sincere physician too.
lines.style: Sincere grateful closing expressing future aspirations inspired by interview.
